One independent author run per case/condition, same frozen inputs and byte-identical runtime. This is a pilot, not evidence of stable improvement.

Grading is coordinator source/image review, not blinded independent grading or human comprehension. Exact author backend model, seed, token counts and elapsed author durations were not returned; all are unknown.

Git: both satisfy all five content assertions. Candidate adds an explicit proposal/evidence/revision table and path-level comparison; baseline uses larger stacked state cards and collapsible references.

Git: neither page overflows at 1280px or 390px. Candidate tables require horizontal scrolling at 390px (keyboard scrolling observed); baseline reflows cards into one column. More explicit review structure is not an unqualified mobile usability win.

Docker: candidate preserves both alternatives as a continuous comparison across all three narration segments; baseline switches to a larger same-RUN diagram in the third segment. Candidate has denser, smaller supporting labels.

Both videos are 638 frames / 21.2667 seconds with identical imported recordings and decoded audio hashes, and identical SRT. Both pass three source A-B-A replay samples and full MP4 decode. These are not semantic-motion or auditory certifications.

Both fail the transition-readability assertion: baseline Visible/Absent labels overlap around frame 318 (10.60s); candidate File visible/Path absent labels overlap around frame 122 (4.07s). Result holds and caption areas are legible in inspected frames, but static endpoint screenshots alone would miss these transitions.

Both plans required a coordinator-only c-base reference association for the visible base-file caveat. Spoken narration and original authored scene sources were unchanged; the initial rejected plan is retained. This common metadata intervention is not candidate benefit.
Full muted browser playback reached the end for both videos. Human listening, pronunciation, precise spoken-cue alignment and learner transfer remain unperformed.

Nine of ten content/visual assertions pass in both conditions; aggregate parity hides structural changes and shared transition defects. Across-case standard deviation is case spread, not repeated-run reliability.

Not covered: independent change-explanation and project-recap tasks, original narration writing, bilingual HTML, other media, broad task generalization. No authored outputs were repaired or promoted into examples.
